# list.plugin.Animate fades the wrong rows when one filter pass adds and removes

## Context

Surfaced 2026-09-18 by the Institution's `FleetGridScaleNL` arm at engine `dev@3f859a4803`: the scenario passes, and the worker-error fixture (`#18554`) reports

```
App Worker: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'style')
    at src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs:645:30   (removedItems.forEach, inside onStoreFilter's timeout)
```

The throw is the loud end of a quiet defect that has been there as long as the method.

## The Problem

`onStoreFilter` splices the **added** rows into `vdom.cn` first, waits 50 ms, then fades the **removed** rows. Outside an interception it resolves a removed row by `obj.index` — its index in `data.oldItems` — against a `vdom.cn` that already holds the added rows:

- old `[alpha, bravo, delta]`, new `[charlie, echo]` → `vdom.cn = [charlie, echo, alpha, bravo, delta]`; the removed rows' old indexes 0/1/2 hit `charlie`, `echo`, `alpha`. **The entering rows fade out, two leaving rows stay fully visible** until the settle pass rebuilds the list.
- If anything rebuilt `vdom.cn` inside those 50 ms (a store load, a sort), the old index points past its end → the `TypeError` above. The added-rows loop two blocks up reads `vdom.cn[index].style` by position the same way.

Removals-only passes (the common narrowing filter) are correct by coincidence: old index equals vdom index.

**Found while writing the arms:** the by-id lookup itself derives the item id from the record KEY (`owner.getItemId(obj.record[key])`, also in the `reAdded` check), while a list with the default `useInternalId: true` builds its item ids from `store.getInternalId(record)`. On such a list the lookup never matches — which is why the moved-rows loop silently does nothing there. The rest of the file already derives it correctly (`owner.getItemId(owner.getRecordId(record))`).

**Found by this ticket's own arms in CI:** `triggerTransitionCallback` arms a raw `setTimeout` and `destroy()` never clears it. A list destroyed inside a transition leaves the timer running; it fires on a plugin whose owner is gone — `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'createItems')` at `Animate.mjs:773` — inside whichever code runs next (in the unit tier: the next test, which is how it showed up as a flake on the first push).

## The Architectural Reality

`src/list/plugin/Animate.mjs` — `onStoreFilter` (`:554`), `getItemIndex(obj, map, intercept)` (`:448`): `intercept` false → positional `obj.index`; true → `map.indexOf(owner.getItemId(key))`. Inside the timeout the method rebuilds `map` from the live `vdom.cn` precisely because "new items are already added into the vdom, while old items are not yet removed", and the moved-rows loop already passes `true` ("honor removed items, even without interceptions"). The added and removed loops beside it do not.

## The Fix

Inside the timeout callback all three loops resolve by id (`getItemIndex(obj, map, true)`): a row is found where it is, and a row that is gone answers `-1` and is skipped. The id comes from `owner.getRecordId(record)`, so internal-id and key-id lists resolve alike. The positional read stays where it is correct — the pre-timeout splice, which needs the *insertion* index.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Red-first unit arm (`test/playwright/unit/list/animatePlugin.spec.mjs`): a filter pass that swaps the visible set fades exactly the leaving rows (opacity 0) and shows exactly the entering ones (opacity 1) during the transition.
- [ ] Red-first unit arm: a list rebuilt inside the 50 ms window throws nothing and fades no surviving row.
- [ ] Red-first unit arm: a list destroyed inside a transition clears its settle timer.
- [ ] The existing filter arms (`filtering fades removed items out…`, `component-list filtering settles…`) stay green.

## Out of Scope

The interception path's own index logic; the sort path (`onStoreSort`); measured row height.

## Avoided Traps

Guarding `vdom.cn[index]?.style` silences the throw and keeps fading the wrong rows.
